Hi Sam — great to meet today.

Quick recap from our discovery call:
- Primary use case: reduce inference cost and latency for Orion product recommendations (latency SLO: <200ms 95th).
- Current infra: in-house GPU fleet + burst to cloud for spikes.
- Decision criteria: predictable latency, lower/unit cost, SOC2 + private deployment option.

Next steps I mentioned on the call:
1) Intro to your economic buyer / budget owner so we can align on pricing model and procurement timeline. You mentioned the potential owner might be Emily Rivers (CFO) — can you confirm?
2) Intro to procurement/legal so we can share a mutual action plan and get any standard T&Cs/questionnaires on file.
3) Short technical follow-up with our SE if helpful (we can do a 30-min session focused on KV caching and batching).

I've attached a short pricing sheet and a draft MAP to make it easier for Emily/procurement to evaluate quickly (ZT-MAP-Redwood.pdf, redwood_pricing_sheet.xlsx). If you can confirm the right procurement contact and Emily's email, I'll draft an intro email and propose a 30-min alignment next week (I have slots Tue/Wed afternoon PT).

Thanks — looking forward to the intro.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa — quick note before the intro:
- Good to offer both committed (discounted) and pilot (short-term, usage) options. Procurement often asks for a pilot PO followed by a committed SKU.
- For the commercial one-pager, call out unit economics (cost per 1k tokens) and the latency SLA options clearly.
- If Emily is the CFO, emphasize predictable spend and fallback policies (we can guarantee a latency window for the dedicated pool).

I'll join the intro as pricing lead if needed. Suggest we open with a 10-min scoping then 20-min commercial/contract discussion.

— Rishi
Director, Solutions & Pricing | Redwood Inference
